key_finding: The FY26 FCF guide of $12.5B is windfall-inflated and Netflix said so itself: the Q1'26 letter raised it from $11B 'due primarily to the after-tax impact of the Warner Bros.-related termination fee'. ORGANIC FY26 FCF guide is ~$11.0B. Striking a yield on $12.5B is 14% too generous.
mode_b_finding: Second engagement-disclosure withdrawal. Subscriber counts stopped in 2025; the Q2'26 letter moves the What We Watched report from semi-annual to ANNUAL beginning 2027, deliberately decoupled from earnings. Mechanism: masking channel = disclosure FREQUENCY on the only metric that decomposes price-led from volume-led growth; signal channel = hours per member; latency = ~9-month blind window, next datapoint Q1'27. It lands in the same letter as the slowest view-hours print (+2% H1'26) and the sharpest deceleration. Graded REVIEW_FLAG not ELEVATE: every contradicting number is on the page (takeaway-vs-data divergence bar not met), and it was a same-day CNBC/Business Insider headline - discovery_state CROWDED, already priced.
anti_masking_finding: Absence of expected masking on the financials is itself a positive: SBC 1.0% of revenue (no non-GAAP bridge), zero contingent claims, the FCF-guide raise SELF-LABELLED as windfall-driven rather than sold as organic strength, the Q2 OI beat attributed by management to expense timing rather than claimed as strength, and the $2.8B fee booked transparently below the operating line. This is a company telling the truth about a decelerating business - the CLEAN pattern, not the catch.
bear_core: Growth switched engines from volume to price and the volume engine is stalled. UCAN (43% of revenue, highest ARPU) printed 10% growth WITH a US price increase in the quarter, down from 18% two quarters earlier. Global view hours +2% H1'26 on a still-growing member base 'approaching 1B' => hours per member are FALLING. Netflix's response - buying creators, podcasts, publisher deals, cloud games - concedes the competitive front is YouTube/short-form, not Disney+.

ai_complex_ruling.court_ruling: AI-ADJACENT, not AI-levered. Courted explicitly against the frozen AI-BREAK|2027-12-31 @ p=0.45.
ai_complex_ruling.detail: No AI capex, no datacentre build, no hyperscaler revenue dependency, no compute-SPV paper. On fundamentals an AI-capex break is mildly FAVOURABLE (cheaper GenAI production tooling, defensive consumer subscription). But the 24x multiple is complex-correlated - assume 18-20x on beta alone in a break. Neither hostage nor hedge: cycle-neutral on fundamentals, cycle-correlated on multiple. Not averaged away.
ai_complex_ruling.portfolio_point: Household already carries ~$5.2M / 26% AI-complex. NFLX adds large-cap growth exposure WITHOUT adding to that concentration - the best non-alpha reason to own it.
ai_complex_ruling.ai_bull: GenAI workflows used in ~300 titles in 2026, concentrated in post-production, 'higher quality output more quickly and at a lower cost' - a specific falsifiable number; Netflix's un-unionised cost base captures this deflation faster than legacy studios. This is the credible path to the 33-34% bull margin.
ai_complex_ruling.ai_bear: Slop/attention war. View hours +2% is its leading indicator and it is already visible.

edge_explainer: The verified de-rate is real: FY26 revenue midpoint ($51.2B), operating margin (31.5%), cash-content/amortisation (1.1x) and organic FCF (~$11B) were all held IDENTICAL across the Q1'26 and Q2'26 letters while the multiple went from ~53x to 24x clean forward. Cap structure is pristine, SBC is 1.0% of revenue so GAAP earnings are the economics, and $27.1B of buyback authorisation (8.7% of cap) is being spent at ~$4.7B/qtr. Netflix also collected $2.8B for LOSING the WBD auction, with no leverage and no integration risk. Against that: the growth rate genuinely reset 5.9pp, UCAN (43% of revenue) printed 10% with a price increase inside it, view hours grew 2%, and the last engagement metric just moved to annual reporting - a ~9-month window in which the decisive variable cannot be checked. There is no informational edge (discovery_state CROWDED - ~50 covering analysts; the guide and the disclosure change were same-day headlines), only a positioning/valuation one worth ~+15.6% to E[FV] over ~18 months, i.e. roughly a market return. That is fairly-paid risk in a verified-honest business at a verified-stable guide: ownable as the deploying book's default class without an edge claim, sleeve-capped at 0.60%, tails bounded and unlevered. The edge overlay is thin and is labelled thin.

Contemporaneous coverage attributes it to a Nasdaq tech selloff under a hawkish new Fed - PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED. Session WebSearch budget exhausted. Cause-check is ~89% complete, not 100%. Beta-bleed carries no information so the ruling is unchanged, but the gap is real.

The Q2'26 buyback average (~high-$80s) is INFERRED from $4.7B across the quarter's traded range. The Q1'26 figure ($96.30 = 13.5M shares / $1.3B) IS exact and disclosed - the 'buyback is not a floor' conclusion holds on that alone.

Ads revenue is NOT separately disclosed in the financial statements - the ~$3B 2026 figure is a management assertion with no auditable line item. K4 is a management-statement trigger, not an XBRL trigger. Weakest-evidenced leg of the bull case.

The termination fee's exact after-tax value is bounded, not pinned: Netflix disclosed a $1.5B FCF-guide delta ($11B -> $12.5B) 'primarily' attributable to a $2.8B pre-tax fee. Organic FCF of ~$11.0B is the company-stated figure (used); the $0.51 EPS clean-up is my estimate.
